newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch court convicts man in insider trading case.
newsitem.headline: Dutch court convicts man in insider trading case.

text.p: A Dutch court has convicted a 38-year-old man for insider trading, fining him 25,000 guilders and confiscating 32,000 guilders in illegal profits, a court spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman said the Amsterdam district court ruled on Friday that the man, identified only by the initials G.K., had used inside information to make a quick trading profit on shares of Dutch industrial springs maker Weweler in late 1993.
The man bought the shares just before Weweler issued a statement saying it no longer expected the sale of a French subsidiary to result in a charge against its earnings.
Once the information was made public, Weweler's share price rose sharply and the defendant -- a son-in-law of a Weweler supervisory director -- sold his shares at a profit.

Prior to the Weweler ruling, there had been only one previous conviction in a Dutch insider trading case, but that was later overturned after a successful appeal. A handful of other cases are still being investigated or are waiting to come to trial.

The Dutch government has said it will tighten up its insider trading law so that prosecutors no longer have to prove that a person made a profit from dealings based on inside information, only that he or she intended to do so. -- Amsterdam newsroom, +31 20504 5000, fax +31 20 504 5000
